Abstract Microenterprises, small enterprises, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) are vital to the economic growth of Indonesia, contributing significantly to employment and national stability. However, many MSMEs struggle with financial management, hindering their growth and access to financing. The implementation of the Financial Accounting Standards for Micro, Small, and Medium Entities (SAK EMKM) was introduced to simplify financial reporting for MSMEs. This study explores the adoption of SAK EMKM at Mutiara Laundry, a case study MSME, to assess its effect on financial transparency, decision-making, and access to external funding. The research highlights challenges such as limited financial literacy and reliance on informal accounting methods. The findings suggest that implementing SAK EMKM enhances financial management and facilitates financing opportunities. The study recommends improving financial literacy and utilizing digital tools to support MSMEs. This research contributes to the understanding of how SAK EMKM can aid MSMEs in improving financial management and long-term sustainability. Practical Implications: The findings of this study highlight that implementing financial statements based on SAK EMKM can significantly enhance the financial management capabilities of micro and small enterprises, such as Mutiara Laundry UMKM. Proper adoption enables business owners to maintain accurate and standardized records, making it easier to monitor performance, control costs, and plan for growth. It also enhances credibility with financial institutions, increasing opportunities for obtaining loans or investments. Social Implications: The adoption of SAK EMKM in micro and small enterprises like Mutiara Laundry UMKM fosters broader social benefits beyond individual business performance. Standardized and transparent financial reporting fosters trust among MSMEs, customers, suppliers, and financial institutions, thereby contributing to the development of stronger local economic ecosystems. Improved financial literacy among small business owners empowers them to make better decisions, sustain their operations, and create more stable employment opportunities in the community. Originality/Value: This study offers a practical contribution by examining the implementation of financial statements based on SAK EMKM in a real-world microenterprise context, using Mutiara Laundry UMKM as a case study. While SAK EMKM is intended to simplify financial reporting for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia, empirical research on its adoption in specific service-sector businesses remains scarce. Keywords: MSMEs, SAK EMKM, financial management, transparency, financing 1. Introduction Microenterprises, small enterprises, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) are fundamental to the economic growth and stability of many countries, including Indonesia. These businesses provide essential employment opportunities, reduce income inequality, and significantly contribute to national economic resilience. According to Law No. 20 of 2008 on MSMEs, these entities are seen as a cornerstone for economic growth, helping to improve living standards and promote social stability (Undang-Undang No. 20, 2008). In Indonesia, MSMEs play a dominant role in the economy. The Ministry of Cooperatives, Micro Enterprises, Industry, and Trade (2021) reported that Indonesia had more than 64 million MSMEs in 2020, representing a substantial portion of the workforce. The significant presence of MSMEs in the retail, food, and service sectors, including laundries, grocery stores, and small restaurants, underscores their crucial role in daily commercial activity (Saifurrahman & Kassim, 2024; Kornelius et al., 2024; Idris, 2019). However, despite their central role, MSMEs face numerous challenges, with financial management being a key issue. Research has shown that MSMEs often struggle with managing finances effectively, which is a major obstacle to their growth and sustainability (Nayla, 2014; Arliman, 2017). Many small businesses lack formal accounting systems, which hinders their ability to track performance accurately and manage financial resources efficiently. This situation is particularly problematic in Multidiscip. Sci. J. The COVID-19 pandemic, which began in 2020, has had a severe impact on MSMEs worldwide. Indonesia was no exception, as the pandemic led to widespread business closures, particularly in the hospitality, retail, and service sectors. Many MSMEs experienced a sharp drop in demand for their services, which, coupled with limited access to financing, threatened their survival (Sujarweni, 2019). For example, many laundromats such as Mutiara Laundry faced reduced demand, as lockdowns and restrictions reduced consumer movement. The financial losses were further exacerbated by the lack of structured financial reporting and poor financial literacy among MSME owners, which made it more difficult to adapt to the crisis (Moleong, 2014). The importance of financial reporting and record-keeping for MSMEs cannot be overstated. Proper financial documentation is not only essential for effective business management but also plays a critical role in securing external funding from banks and other financial institutions. According to Hery (2019), financial transparency is crucial for businesses to build trust with financial institutions and investors. However, many MSME owners do not have the necessary skills or knowledge to create formal financial statements; instead, they rely on simple and informal bookkeeping methods. This lack of formal financial reporting is a significant barrier to accessing credit and loans (Harun et al., 2015; Al et al., 2025; Idris & Bahasoan, 2025). To address these challenges, the Indonesian Institute of Accountants (IAI) introduced the Financial Accounting Standards for Micro, Small, and Medium Entities (SAK EMKM) in 2016, which took effect on January 1, 2018. SAK EMKM was developed to simplify financial reporting for MSMEs, enabling them to prepare structured and standardized financial statements without the complexity of traditional accounting standards. The implementation of SAK EMKM is expected to help MSMEs improve their financial transparency, increase their credibility, and ultimately gain better access to financing (IAI, 2016). SAK EMKM consists of a simplified version of accounting standards that align with the operational realities of small businesses, including specific guidelines on how to report assets, liabilities, equity, income, and expenses (Hoang & Bui, 2023; Kornelius et al., 2024; Waoma et al., 2024; Waoma et al., 2024). One example of an MSME that could benefit from the adoption of SAK EMKM is Mutiara Laundry, a small laundry service business established in January 2023 by Hj. Sukawati. Despite its operational success, Mutiara Laundry’s financial management remains rudimentary, with records primarily limited to manual daily entries of income and expenses. Although the business has access to a mobile app with features for financial management, employees do not utilize the app effectively because of a lack of training and financial literacy (Sularsih & Sobir, 2019). This situation is not unique; previous studies have shown that many MSMEs in Indonesia, such as Silky Parijatah, also face challenges in adopting formal accounting practices. Mutiah (2019) ported that businesses such as Silky Parijatah used simple bookkeeping methods and did not prepare financial statements in accordance with SAK EMKM. Similarly, Yuli and Oswald (2019) noted that none of the 74 MSMEs they surveyed in Malalayang II were complying with accounting standards due to limited awareness and the perceived complexity of the process. This lack of compliance with proper accounting standards significantly limits MSMEs’ ability to secure external funding, as financial institutions require detailed and accurate financial reports to assess business viability. According to Bank Indonesia (2015), MSMEs that fail to provide formal financial documentation often struggle to access bank loans. In fact, the absence of a structured financial reporting system is a key reason why banks remain cautious about extending credit to MSMEs, despite policies that encourage lending to small businesses (Hasanuddin & Islianty, 2017; Idris, 2019). The implementation of SAK EMKM represents a promising solution to these issues. By adopting these simplified standards, MSMEs can improve their financial reporting practices, enhance their ability to obtain credit, attract investment, and achieve long-term sustainability. Research conducted by (Widiastoeti & Sari, 2020) supports this view, showing that MSMEs that adopted SAK EMKM experienced improvements in financial transparency, which facilitated better decision-making and improved access to financing. Moreover, the standard's emphasis on simplicity and ease of use makes it a practical option for MSMEs with limited resources and financial expertise (Ardiansyah, 2022). This study aims to explore the application of SAK EMKM at Mutiara Laundry, a case study of an MSME that faces challenges related to financial management. By examining the effects of structured financial reporting on decision-making and business sustainability, this research contributes to the broader understanding of how SAK EMKM can help MSMEs improve their financial management and long-term viability. Additionally, this study will identify the barriers to adopting SAK EMKM and propose solutions to enhance financial literacy among MSME owners and employees. 2. Literature Review 2.1. Implementation of SAK EMKM in SMEs The implementation of SAK EMKM is expected to facilitate SMEs in preparing financial statements that are simpler, less complicated, and more relevant and transparent, especially in the context of access to financing and better business management. This standard is tailored to the characteristics of SMEs, which face limitations in capacity, technology, and accounting knowledge that can be complex. SAK EMKM was introduced by the Indonesian Institute of Accountants (IAI) with the aim that SMEs could manage their financial statements in a more practical manner, in line with recognized accounting standards, thus making it easier for them https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Idrus and Rastina (2026) 3 to access financing from financial institutions and be more reliable in decision-making by external parties such as investors or creditors. This implementation has been in effect since January 1, 2018, and has been proven to provide clear guidance for preparing financial statements in accordance with the capacity of SMEs (Zulfikar et al., 2022). However, although SAK EMKM aims to simplify the accounting process, in practice, many SMEs still face difficulties in fully implementing it. (Zulfikar et al., 2022) emphasized that the SAK EMKM is designed with a higher level of than other standards, such as SAK-ETAP, which is more suitable for larger entities. By using a historical cost-based approach, this standard allows SMEs to more easily understand and implement it without the need for a complex accounting system. This is also supported by (Mukhlisin et al., 2022), who stated that SAK EMKM focuses on basic transactions that frequently occur in SMEs, such as purchases, sales, and expenditures, making it easier to record and monitor finances. 2.2. Challenges in Implementing SAK EMKM Despite the ease with which SAK EMKM is offered, its implementation among SMEs in Indonesia remains relatively low. Research by Mutiah (2019) revealed that financial record-keeping at Silky Parijatah, a trading business in Banyuwangi, is still very simple. Only purchases and sales are recorded without preparing formal financial statements that comply with standards. This reflects a lack of understanding of the importance of financial statements and a lack of awareness about SAK EMKM among SME owners, which ultimately hinders transparent and accurate financial management. A study by Rawun & Tumilaar (2019) also reported similar results in Malalayang District, Manado. Among the 74 SMEs registered, none prepared financial statements according to SAK EMKM. This study suggests that a lack of time and knowledge is the main barrier for SMEs in adopting SAK EMKM effectively. Most SMEs perceive that more formal and structured accounting processes require significant time and effort, whereas they prefer to focus on their business operations, which they consider more urgent. 2.3. Accounting Literacy Limitations in SMEs Research by (Widiastoeti & Sari, 2020) revealed that in the Kampung Kue SME in Rungkut, Surabaya, most SME owners maintain only simple records without any consistent or regular system of bookkeeping. These irregular and incomplete records make it difficult to ensure the accuracy of financial information. This highlights one of the greatest challenges in implementing SAK EMKM: the lack of accounting literacy among SME owners. Most SME owners in Indonesia come from backgrounds that do not focus on accounting education. As a result, they struggle to understand the basic accounting principles that should be applied in preparing financial statements in accordance with the applicable standards. The lack of trained human resources in accounting, coupled with an understanding of the importance of accurate and transparent financial statements, presents a significant obstacle to the development of SMEs themselves. Support in accounting education and training is necessary to help SME owners understand and implement SAK EMKM more effectively. Several training programs provided by the government and financial institutions can offer broader insights into the importance of structured financial statements that comply with standards. 2.4. The Importance of Implementing SAK EMKM for Access to Financing The implementation of SAK EMKM is useful not only for improving transparency and accountability but also for facilitating SMEs' access to bank financing. (Sudharma & Gorda, 2021) explained that the SME sector plays a strategic role in the national economy but is often hindered by the inability to prepare financial statements that meet standards, which is one of the main requirements for applying for loans at banks. Therefore, with the implementation of SAK EMKM, SMEs are expected to have easier access to financing and experience faster growth. Additionally, SAK EMKM helps SME owners manage cash flow and monitor their financial performance more effectively. With good financial statements, business owners can make more informed decisions regarding business expansion, the purchase of raw materials, or marketing strategies, all of which affect the sustainability and growth of their business. 3. The Role of Financial Statements in the Growth of SMEs Financial statements are not just records of numbers or transactions conducted by SMEs. These statements are crucial tools for assessing financial performance and providing a clear picture of the financial health of a business. Therefore, financial statements function as an evaluation of business performance, helping business owners in planning strategic decisions such as cash management, expense planning, and decisions for business expansion. According to (Yusuf & Ichsan, 2021), good financial performance reflects the results of a company’s economic activities during a specific period and is vital for predicting its financial condition in the future. This performance can be seen through various financial statements, such as income statements, balance sheets (financial position statements), and cash flow statements. All of these reports provide a deeper understanding of how well a business can manage its revenues and expenditures effectively and efficiently. Without structured financial statements, it is very difficult for business owners to determine whether their business is making a profit or incurring a loss. Additionally, financial statements play a vital role in accessing financing, whether from banks, investors, or other financial institutions. Many SMEs struggle to obtain loans or external funding because they cannot provide financial statements that https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Idrus and Rastina (2026) 4 meet the standards required by lending institutions. Without clear financial reports, lenders find it difficult to assess an SME's ability to repay loans or determine the viability of the business for receiving additional capital. 3.1. Challenges faced by SMEs in Preparing Financial Statements Although financial statements are crucial for the growth and sustainability of SMEs, many SME owners are still unaware of the importance of preparing good financial statements. (Budiarto et al., 2023) reported that most SME owners do not realize how important financial statements are for the continuity of their business. This is mostly due to the limited education and accounting knowledge held by the owners or managers of SMEs. As a result, the financial statements produced are often not up to standard and cannot be used as a solid basis for decision-making or as requirements for loan applications. In many cases, SME owners are more focused on daily operations and short-term survival rather than viewing financial statements as tools for long-term planning. This creates a significant problem because, without proper financial statements, SMEs struggle to plan for expansion or even manage the risks their businesses face. 3.2. The Benefits of Financial Statements for Business Owners and Other Stakeholders According to (Budiarto et al., 2023), financial statements are useful not only for business owners but also for other parties involved in decision-making, such as investors and creditors. For business owners, financial statements provide an overview of how profitable and efficient their business is. This allows business owners to adjust strategies or operational policies to improve profitability. Investors also use financial statements to assess the growth potential and risks involved in investing in an SME. Transparent and structured reports help investors make more informed decisions about whether to increase their investment. On the other hand, creditors rely on financial statements to assess whether an SME has enough assets and the ability to repay its debts. Without clear and trustworthy financial reports, creditors find it difficult to assess the financial health of SMEs, leading to many loan applications being rejected. 3.3. Financial Statements as a Strategic Planning Tool In addition to serving as an evaluation tool and access to financing, financial statements also function as a strategic planning instrument for SMEs. By having accurate and up-to-date financial reports, business owners can more easily plan business expansion, manage cash flow, and make adjustments to inefficient operations (Stonehouse & Pemberton, 2002). The income statement, for example, provides an overview of revenues and expenses over a specific period. This provides important information about whether a business is experiencing profit or loss and what factors contribute to those results. (Aldehayyat et al., 2011) The balance sheet or financial position statement provides an understanding of the assets and liabilities held by the business at a given time, helping owners determine whether they have enough capital to finance operations and expansion. With proper financial statements, SME owners can identify areas that need improvement, such as wasteful expenditure management or suboptimal revenue collection. This enables them to make more informed decisions, not only on the basis of intuition or estimates (Rejison, 2025). 4. Banking Support and Financial Access for SMEs Banking plays a crucial role in strengthening the micro, small-, and medium-sized enterprise (SME) sector. SMEs are often seen as the backbone of the economy because of their significant contribution to job creation, gross domestic product (GDP) growth, and local economic empowerment. Therefore, access to financing becomes a critical factor in supporting the growth and sustainability of SMEs. Bank Indonesia, through Circular Letter No. 17/19/DPUM in 2015, set a minimum target for credit distribution to SMEs at 20% of total bank loans, which has been effective since 2018. The aim of this policy is to strengthen the capacity of SMEs to access funds from financial institutions so that they can expand their businesses and enhance their competitiveness. However, significant obstacles remain in achieving this target. As noted in Tarizza’s thesis (2024), many SMEs face difficulties in obtaining financing from banks, mainly because they are unable to present structured financial statements that meet the standards required by financial institutions. Without clear, transparent, and compliant financial statements, it is challenging for banks to assess the creditworthiness and associated risks of lending to SMEs.(Saifurrahman & Kassim, 2024) According to Arliman (2017), SMEs play a very strategic role in the national economy; therefore, they need policies that focus more on empowerment and support this sector. Policies aimed at strengthening financial literacy, preparing proper financial statements, and educating on the implementation of SAK EMKM (Indonesian Financial Accounting Standards for Micro, Small, and Medium Entities) are crucial for enabling SMEs to become more independent in managing their finances and easier-to-access funding from banks or other financial institutions. Properly prepared financial statements, in accordance with SAK EMKM, are a key requirement for SMEs to obtain financing from financial institutions. With transparent financial reports, banks and investors can more easily assess the financial performance and potential risks of SMEs, enabling them to make better decisions regarding credit or funding provisions. https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Idrus and Rastina (2026) 5 5. Challenges in Implementing SAK EMKM Although SAK EMKM is designed to help SMEs prepare simpler and standardized financial statements, its implementation in the field still faces various challenges. These challenges can be categorized into two main groups: internal challenges and external challenges. 5.1. Internal challenges According to (Dewi & Prawira, 2019), internal challenges for SMEs include several factors that limit their ability to implement SAK EMKM optimally, such as limited capital, human resources (HR), and low accountability. Many SME owners still use simple and manual bookkeeping methods that do not meet the accounting standards recommended in SAK EMKM. This is largely due to the lack of awareness among SME owners about the importance of good financial reporting and the absence of competent human resources in accounting. In addition, capital limitations are a significant challenge for SMEs in implementing SAK EMKM. They tend to focus more on daily operations and find it difficult to allocate enough resources to prepare more formal financial statements. Under these conditions, many SMEs prefer to use simple methods to record transactions and lack a structured accounting system. 5.2. External challenges In addition to internal challenges, external challenges, such as limited infrastructure and access to adequate technology, affect the success of implementing SAK EMKM. SMEs often face constraints in terms of facilities and infrastructure, particularly in underdeveloped areas. Without access to appropriate technology, it is difficult for SMEs to adopt accounting systems based on software or financial applications that can help them prepare financial statements more efficiently. These limitations are further exacerbated by a lack of technological knowledge among SME owners. For example, although some SMEs use cash register applications that provide complete bookkeeping features, many SME owners do not maximize the use of these features, as found in Tarizza’s research (2024) at Mutiara Laundry. For example, Mutiara Laundry still performs manual bookkeeping and records only daily income and expenses without preparing more comprehensive financial statements. In fact, the application they use has the potential to help them manage more complete financial reports that comply with SAK EMKM. 6. Materials and Methods Research Type, This study utilizes a descriptive qualitative research method aimed at exploring and analyzing the implementation of financial statements on the basis of SAK EMKM in Mutiara Laundry MSME. This research type is chosen to understand in detail how SAK EMKM is implemented and to identify challenges faced by MSME owners in applying the accounting standard. Research Approach: A qualitative research approach was employed, with a focus on collecting data through interviews, observations, and document analysis. This approach enables an in-depth understanding of the implementation process of financial reporting on the basis of SAK EMKM at Mutiara Laundry MSME and the factors that influence its adoption. Research location: This research was conducted at Mutiara Laundry MSME, which is located in Makassar city, South Sulawesi. This MSME was selected because of its potential to benefit from adopting SAK EMKM in financial reporting, yet it had not yet fully implemented the standard. Data Sources: The data used in this study include both primary and secondary sources: primary data: These data were collected directly from interviews, observations, and document analysis conducted at Mutiara Laundry MSME. The primary data include information gathered through conversations with the owner and employees, as well as observations of daily operations and financial record-keeping practices. Secondary Data: These data were obtained from the internal documents of Mutiara Laundry MSME, including existing transaction records and financial statements, as well as relevant literature on the application of SAK EMKM to MSMEs. Data collection techniques: The following data collection techniques were used in this study: In-depth interviews were conducted with the owners and employees of Mutiara Laundry MSME. The goal was to understand their financial recording practices, their knowledge of SAK EMKM, and the challenges faced in implementing financial statements according to the standard. This aligns with the techniques suggested by Sugiyono (2019), who stated that interviews are a key strategy in qualitative research. Observations: Direct observations were conducted at the Mutiara Laundry MSME site. The researcher observed daily operations and financial management practices to gain insight into how transactions are recorded and whether formal accounting systems were in place. This observation technique is supported by (Inayatul, 2015), who emphasized the importance of direct observation in qualitative research. Documentation: Document analysis was used to collect secondary data, including transaction records, income, and expenditure reports, as well as other relevant financial documents. According to (Sugiono, 2012), documentation is an essential technique to support research findings. Data analysis Techniques: The data analysis in this study uses descriptive qualitative analysis, following the following steps: Data collection: Data were gathered from interviews, observations, and documentation. Data Categorization: The data were categorized into themes such as financial transaction recording, SAK EMKM adoption, challenges faced, and proposed solutions. This categorization process allows for the identification of emerging patterns and insights. Data Interpretation: The https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Idrus and Rastina (2026) 6 categorized data were analyzed to understand the underlying factors that affect the implementation of SAK EMKM in Mutiara Laundry MSME. Iwan (2020) discussed the importance of correctly interpreting financial transactions in line with standards. Data validity To ensure the validity and reliability of the data, triangulation was applied. This technique involves combining multiple data collection methods (interviews, observations, and documentation) to verify the consistency and accuracy of the findings, as recommended by (Sugiono, 2012). 7. Results 7.1. Overview of Multiara Laundry Mutiara Laundry is a microbusiness established in January 2023 that offers various laundry services, such as washing, ironing, dry cleaning, and specialty services for items such as blankets, carpets, and even shoes. The laundry is located in a residential complex in Bulurokeng, Makassar, providing easy access for local customers. The business operates daily from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM, with a steady flow of customers, particularly from the surrounding community. The business started with a single washing machine and a basic ironing set, and over time, as customer demand increased, the business expanded both in terms of its service offerings and workforce. Despite the growing customer base and operational complexity, Mutiara Laundry’s financial management system remained underdeveloped. The owner, Ibu Hj Sukawati, initially relied on a manual bookkeeping system and recorded daily income and expenses. However, no formal financial reports, such as balance sheets or income statements, were generated. This lack of formal financial reporting limits the owner’s ability to evaluate the business's financial performance, which is critical for making informed business decisions. Without accurate records, the business faced challenges in assessing profitability, managing cash flow, and securing external funding, such as bank loans. Reliance on informal and manual accounting practices was not uncommon among small businesses, as highlighted by previous studies. Mutia (2019) reported that similar businesses in Banyuwangi, such as Silky Parijatah, faced difficulties due to their simplified accounting practices, which hindered their ability to make informed financial decisions. Similarly, observed that MSMEs in Malalayang II, Manado, failed to comply with formal accounting standards, which led to inefficiencies in financial management and difficulty accessing credit. 7.2. Financial Reporting Issues The research revealed that Mutiara Laundry’s financial recording practices were significantly below the standards required for MSMEs in Indonesia, specifically those outlined by the SAK EMKM (Financial Accounting Standards for Micro, Small and Medium Entities). The business's financial reporting was confined to basic manual records, mainly tracking cash inflows and outflows without accounting for other crucial financial elements, such as assets, liabilities, or equity. The absence of formal financial reports meant that Mutiara Laundry was unable to track the following: 1. Profitability: The business lacked an income statement, making it difficult to assess how much profit was being generated from its operations. This is essential for understanding the sustainability of a business and whether it is financially viable in the long term. 2. Financial Position: Without a balance sheet, the business cannot clearly assess its assets, liabilities, and equity. This information is essential for understanding the financial health of the business, particularly in regard to managing debts and planning for future investments. 3. Cash Flow: The absence of formal accounting records meant that the business had no clear view of its cash flow, which is critical for ensuring that the business can meet its short-term obligations and invest in growth. In this context, (Vovchenko et al., 2017)noted that many MSMEs do not maintain proper accounting records and do not understand the importance of formal financial statements for managing cash flow and profitability. Their study revealed that MSMEs that failed to adopt standard accounting practices had poor financial planning and were often unprepared for economic challenges, making them vulnerable to financial instability. 7.3. Implementation of the SAK EMKM The implementation of SAK EMKM would significantly improve the quality and accuracy of Mutiara Laundry’s financial reporting. This accounting standard is specifically designed for MSMEs in Indonesia, providing a simplified framework for financial reporting that helps businesses meet regulatory requirements and improve transparency. Key Components of SAK EMKM Implementation. The adoption of SAK EMKM for Mutiara Laundry involves the preparation of the following key financial statements: 7.3.1. Balance Sheet (Laporan Posisi Keuangan) The balance sheet is a snapshot of a company’s financial position at a specific point in time, summarizing its assets, liabilities, and equity. For Mutiara Laundry, implementing a balance sheet would provide an accurate picture of the business’s financial health. It would allow the owner to track current and noncurrent assets, liabilities, and equity. The balance sheet https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Idrus and Rastina (2026) 7 would be instrumental in assessing liquidity (the ability to meet short-term obligations) and solvency (the ability to meet long- term obligations). 7.3.2. Income Statement (Laporan Laba Rugi) The income statement summarizes a company’s revenues, expenses, and profits over a specific period (usually one year). For Mutiara Laundry, an income statement would provide critical insights into its profitability by showing the difference between total revenues and operational costs. This report can help the owner assess whether the business is generating enough income to cover expenses and generate profits. By using this financial statement, Mutiara Laundry could also identify areas where costs could be reduced or where revenue generation strategies could be enhanced. 7.3.3. Statement of Changes in Equity (Laporan Perubahan Modal) This financial statement outlines changes in the owner’s equity over time, including additions from retained earnings or capital contributions and deductions from withdrawals or losses. For Mutiara Laundry, the statement of changes in equity would help the owner track the business’s growth by showing how profits are reinvested into the business or withdrawn for personal use. By adopting SAK EMKM, Mutiara Laundry would be able to generate formal and standardized reports that provide a more accurate reflection of the business’s financial performance. This will ultimately help the business make more informed decisions, such as adjusting prices, reducing costs, or expanding service offerings. 7.4. Conclusions On the basis of the analysis and findings of this study regarding the financial reporting practices at Mutiara Laundry, the business’s current financial management system is clearly underdeveloped. The business has been using a very simple and manual bookkeeping system, where only daily income and expenses are recorded, without generating formal financial reports such as income statements or balance sheets. This method has created significant limitations for the owner, particularly in evaluating the business’s financial performance, assessing profitability, managing cash flow, and making informed decisions for future growth. Without accurate financial records, the business also faces difficulties in securing external funding or obtaining loans from financial institutions. The study reveals that Mutiara Laundry's financial reporting practices are far from meeting the standards outlined in the SAK EMKM (Standards of Financial Accounting for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises) established in Indonesia. The absence of formal financial statements has left the business without a clear understanding of its financial position and performance, which could hinder its growth and sustainability in the long run. This research further emphasizes the importance of adopting the SAK EMKM framework, which is specifically designed for MSMEs in Indonesia. Implementing SAK EMKM would not only streamline the financial reporting process but also provide a standardized framework that ensures the accuracy, transparency, and consistency of financial statements. By adopting these standards, Mutiara Laundry would be able to generate key financial reports, such as balance sheets, income statements, and statements of changes in equity, that would offer valuable insights into its financial health. This would help the owner monitor cash flow, assess profitability, manage liabilities, and make more informed business decisions. The research suggests that Mutiara Laundry should begin using SAK EMKM to prepare its financial reports. This adoption helps businesses track their financial performance more effectively, improves their decision-making processes, and enhances their ability to secure financing from external sources, which is essential for expansion and long-term sustainability. In addition, Mutiara Laundry should make better use of available tools, such as the Mini Laundry Cashier application, which provides various features that could assist in improving the management and reporting of finances. Moreover, the owner and employees must improve their understanding of accounting practices. Providing training or seeking support from accounting professionals could help businesses implement a more formal and structured accounting system. This would not only lead to better financial management but also increase the business’s credibility and competitiveness in the market. In conclusion, implementing formal financial reporting practices via SAK EMKM will significantly benefit Mutiara Laundry, helping it improve its financial management, decision-making, and long-term growth potential. This approach is not only a necessary step for ensuring the business’s financial health but also a strategic move toward greater financial transparency and access to funding, which are critical for scaling and maintaining a successful MSME in today’s competitive market environment. JSON: Name: sak_emkm_mutiara Title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of SAK EMKM implementation to improve financial reporting completeness and access to external financing in a micro laundry MSME Short Hypothesis: Implementing SAK EMKM-compliant financial statements together with basic accounting training increases financial reporting completeness by at least 25% and increases the loan approval rate by at least 10 percentage points for Mutiara Laundry within 12 months relative to pre-implementation and matched control MSMEs. Related Work: Existing work documents low adoption of simplified accounting standards among MSMEs, frequent reliance on informal/manual bookkeeping, and associations between structured reporting and improved transparency. Prior interventions include awareness campaigns, one-off trainings, and introduction of bookkeeping apps; these studies report positive but heterogeneous self-reported outcomes. Limitations across prior work are (1) predominance of cross-sectional or descriptive designs, (2) small convenience samples and sector-limited case reports, (3) reliance on subjective survey measures rather than objective financial records or loan outcomes, (4) lack of controlled or longitudinal evaluation to attribute causal impact, and (5) limited assessment of digital tool uptake and combined effects of training plus software. There is therefore limited causal evidence quantifying SAK EMKM's effect on measurable financial metrics and formal financing outcomes in service-sector MSMEs. Abstract: MSMEs commonly lack standardized financial reporting, limiting internal decision-making and access to formal financing. This research implements SAK EMKM-compliant financial statements at Mutiara Laundry combined with targeted accounting training and optional digital bookkeeping, and evaluates effects on objective financial-reporting quality and external financing outcomes. The approach uses a quasi-experimental pre–post design with matched control MSMEs and an ablation comparing training-only versus training-plus-digital-tool arms. Main contributions are (1) objective measurement of reporting completeness, accuracy, and regularity using transaction-level records, (2) quantification of changes in financial ratios and loan application and approval outcomes, and (3) an empirical comparison of training versus training+software. Expected outcomes are improved statement completeness and timeliness, measurable improvements in selected financial ratios, and higher rates of successful loan approvals for treated firms. Results will provide evidence on the practical impact of SAK EMKM adoption and inform policy and practitioner support strategies for MSME financial reporting. Experiments: Study design: quasi-experimental pre–post with matched controls and two treatment variants. Units: Mutiara Laundry (deep case) plus 30 additional micro-laundries in Makassar, matched by monthly revenue, years operating, and customer volume. Random assignment at enterprise level into three arms where possible: (A) control (status quo, n=10), (B) training-only (SAK EMKM training and templates, n=10), (C) training + digital bookkeeping app configured for SAK EMKM (n=10, includes Mutiara Laundry if practical). Data: transaction-level records, cashier logs, bank statements, loan application records, and monthly operational reports for 12 months pre-intervention and 12 months post-intervention. Baselines: existing manual bookkeeping (status quo), and alternative intervention (training-only) serve as baselines for the combined intervention. Metrics: primary—reporting completeness score (proportion of required SAK EMKM line items reported monthly), reporting accuracy (reconciliation error rate between bank statements and reported cash), reporting timeliness (days between month-end and report availability); secondary—financial ratios (net profit margin, current ratio, operating cash flow margin), number of loan applications submitted, loan approval rate, average approved loan amount, and simple decision-making indicators (frequency of recorded investment or price changes). Evaluation: difference-in-differences estimation comparing pre/post changes between arms, mixed-effects panel regressions with enterprise fixed effects and month fixed effects, clustered standard errors at enterprise level, significance threshold α=0.05. Ablation: compare outcomes of arm B (training-only) versus arm C (training+app) to isolate digital tool effect. Robustness: propensity score matching for imperfect randomization, placebo tests on pre-intervention trends, and sensitivity analyses excluding outliers. Data collection cadence: monthly aggregation; duration: 24 months (12 pre, 12 post). Risk Factors and Limitations: Selection bias and limited external validity due to small sample and single-city/service-sector focus; nonrandom assignment if enterprises decline randomization, reducing causal inference strength. Hawthorne effect and temporary behavior change from monitoring. Variable compliance and heterogeneous uptake of training or digital tools across firms producing wide treatment effect heterogeneity. Data quality issues: missing or inconsistent transaction logs, informal cash transactions not recorded, and reconciliation errors. Confounding external shocks (seasonality, local policy changes, macroeconomic shocks, or pandemic resurgence) may affect financial outcomes independently of treatment. Measurement bias in loan outcomes due to bank credit policy changes or relationship lending not captured by firm-level records. Limited follow-up (12 months) may be insufficient to observe long-term financing or growth outcomes. Ethical/privacy constraints on sharing detailed financial records may restrict reproducibility. Scalability limitations: operational support required for training and app deployment may not generalize to resource-constrained settings.
